Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
142 PM PST Wed Nov 18 2026

.SYNOPSIS...18/104 PM.

Cool, below normal temperatures will be ongoing through the week.
A moderate to strong low pressure system will bring gusty winds, 
widespread rain, mountain snow, and a chance for thunderstorms 
Wednesday into Thursday. There is a risk of significant impacts, 
including a flooding and the potential for wind related issues. 
Very large surf and high tides will continue, with ongoing surf 
and flooding hazards at the coast.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SAT)...18/141 PM.

All systems are a go for a moderate to strong storm system moving
into the area today for the Central Coast and working its way 
south through tonight and tomorrow morning. The storm has been 
producing rain rates just over 1 inch per hour in the Bay Area 
this morning even without thunderstorms which still remain 
offshore. And the latest high res models are very similar to 
earlier runs so confidence is high this will be an impactful 
storm.

During the peak periods of rain, rates will easily reach a half 
inch per hour, with areas of 0.75" per hour and localized areas 
of 1 inch per hour. These highest rates will most likely occur in 
the mountains, with the best chances in the Santa Barbara and 
western Ventura Mountains. Storm totals remain about the same, 1-2
inches most coast/valley areas, locally up to 3 inches in areas
with the highest rain rates, most notably parts of southern Santa
Barbara County. South facing slopes 2-5".

This storm is expected to be very convective when the strongest
part of the storm moves through so expect to see around 2-4 hours
of thunderstorms in most areas. Along with that, there is a very
small chance, 5% or less, of a weak tornado with the best chances
of that in the LA Basin on Thursday.

During the heaviest part of the storm wind gusts up to 35 mph are
possible at lower elevations and up to 50 mph in the mountains.
For this reason, it would be prudent to avoid parking vehicles 
under trees and being mindful of any heavy patio furniture. There 
is a flood watch in all areas except the Antelope Valley, so 
expect streets and freeways to be very wet and slick and at times 
un-passable.

Freezing levels will remain above 7500 feet for all but the last
few hours of the storm, during which 3-6 inches could fall mostly
above 7000 feet. Due to the very high elevation and limited
impacts no snow related products will be issued.

Dry weather will return Friday and Saturday with light offshore
flow and highs mostly in the 60s.

.LONG TERM (SUN-WED)...18/312 AM.

A little pop up ridge moves through the state on Saturday. It will
make it a dry day with sunny skies. Despite the ridge and sunshine
max temps will not change much and will remain 5 to 10 degrees blo
normal.

Mdls have sped up the next system. It is not very strong it will
likely bring rain to the Central Coast, but will only have about a
40 percent chc of bringing rain to areas south of Pt Conception.
Up to a quarter inch of rain may fall across the Central Coast. If
rain does make it south of Pt Conception, rainfall totals will not
exceed a tenth of an inch. Max temps will continue in the mid 60s.

Another pop up ridge will cross the area Monday. Dry and mostly
sunny conditions will prevail. Temps will not change much.

Not the best agreement within all of the various mdls but another
system seems possible later next Tuesday or Wednesday. There is a
20 percent chc that this could be a decent sized system.

&&

.AVIATION...18/1736Z.

At 1717Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Generally moderate confidence in TAFs. High confidence in periods
of gusty south to west winds with -SHRA to RA starting this 
afternoon, continuing through the period. Northern areas will see 
gusty winds and rain first, with impacts moving south through 
tonight. Lower confidence in timing (+/- 3 hours) and magnitude of
winds and rain. Brief heavy downpours are likely across portions 
of the area, with LIFR to IFR vsbys possible in heavier rains.

There is a 20% chance of thunderstorms through the period,
starting this afternoon.
KLAX...Good confidence in TAF through 06Z. Aft 06Z-12Z there is a
30 percent chc of 4SM -RA BKN025 conds. From 12Z to 18Z there is
30 percent chc of 3SM -RA BKN015 conds. There is a 20 percent chc
of a TSTM after 12Z. There is a 40 percent chc of an 8 to 10 kt 
east wind component after 08Z.

KBUR...Good confidence in TAF through 06Z. Aft 06Z-12Z there is a
30 percent chc of 4SM -RA BKN025 conds. There is a 20 percent chc
of a TSTM after 12Z.

&&

.MARINE...18/124 PM.

High confidence in dangerous ocean conditions through Friday due 
to a combination of gusty winds and large seas. Conditions are
beginning to deteriorate and will continue to do so through today
as another storm system is moving into the coastal waters. Gale 
Warnings are in effect for the nearshore and outer waters 
adjacent to the Central Coast. Gale force winds will still be 
possible elsewhere but will likely remain more localized. Along 
with gusty SW to NW winds, seas will continue to increase due to 
the combination of a large northwest swell and southwest wind 
swell. Large breaking waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor and to a 
lesser extent Ventura Harbor from Wednesday through Thursday. 
Additionally, Pismo and Cayucos may see breaking waves at or over 
the base of the piers.

The storm system will bring widespread moderate to locally heavy 
rain, along with the potential for thunderstorms with gusty winds,
heavy downpours, and lightning through Thursday afternoon.

Conditions will improve through the day Friday and become relatively
mild through Saturday. Another storm system is possible as early 
as next Sunday, thus another round of dangerous winds and seas is 
possible later into Sunday.

&&

.BEACHES...18/124 PM.

Dangerous conditions continue across the beach starting today and
continuing into Friday, peaking tonight through Thursday. 

Large surf will create very dangerous rip currents and jetty
conditions. Additionally, minor to moderate coastal flooding 
issues may occur, especially on Thursday during peak morning high 
tide. Some impacts may be shallow seawater flooding over low lying
beaches/walkways/parking lots and significant beach erosion. 
Impacts along the Central Coast will likely be higher such as 
localized wave damage (especially to piers, localized coastal 
flooding impacting roads and possibly structures, as well as 
breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor.

High Surf Advisories have been issued for all beach areas. A 
Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect for the Central Coast for 
Thursday.

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional swells are becoming increasingly likely next week as
well. These swells may produce period of elevated to high surf.
The combination of very high tides and increasing surf will likely
lead to at least widespread moderate coastal flooding issues 
across all coasts. There is potential for significant coastal
flooding impacts if a larger swell brings significant surf to the
area on top of the extreme tides.
